supersededNote: Snapshot of HEAD 50cbfc0 before the 2026-09-08 FIX remediations. Findings describe that revision, not later working-tree changes (README alignment, video role=img, sensor contrast, versioned poster preload, reduced-motion poster handoff, favicon, UltraTransition teardown, pin-on-fail).

findings.title: Named <video> elements use an invalid ARIA role=img
rebuttalsChecked: role=img on canvas is allowed — not the defect; canvas in ScrubStage is out of scope
Decorative videos omit the role via aria-hidden — true, but Hero and every LazyVideo with alt still set role=img
Lab desktop Lighthouse scored aria-allowed-role as 1 despite items — live desktop/mobile reports score 0; ARIA in HTML still forbids role=img on video

evidence.detail: Hero <video> sets role="img" plus aria-label.
role={decorative ? undefined : 'img'} when alt is provided.
aria-allowed-role score 0; first item is the hero video: ARIA role img is not allowed for given element.
Same axe items on localhost:3100 for Hero, FeatureFilm, Dynamic Island, Aperture, C2, Battery, Ultra transition videos.

findings.impact: Assistive tech may ignore or mishandle the accessible name on the hero and other labelled clips. Live Lighthouse still fails aria-allowed-role.
findings.remediation: Remove role="img" from <video>. Keep aria-label (or a visually adjacent caption) so the clip remains named. Leave canvas role="img" as-is.

findings.title: Camera-sensor callout indices fail WCAG AA contrast
rebuttalsChecked: Lab contrast hits on --bone-faint #55534f are stale — current global.scss raises --bone-faint to #8a8780 (~5.8:1 on black); those items were rejected
Callout body copy uses --bone and passes; the index is extra chrome — true, but 01–05 are still visible 11px / 8.3pt text at ~2.5:1
Could be large text — rejected: live report lists 8.3pt / 11px normal weight
Desktop lab missed the indices — they are opacity 0 while pinned; live mobile stacked layout exposes them

evidence.detail: .calloutIndex { color: var(--cherry-hi); } on a near-black label chip.
--cherry-hi: #71405b.
color-contrast score 0 on CameraSensor_calloutIndex: 2.5:1 (#71405b on #050507), expected 4.5:1.

findings.impact: Low-vision users cannot reliably read the 01–05 indices on the sensor legend, especially on the mobile stacked video-tier layout where those numbers sit in the flow.
findings.remediation: Color the index with --bone, --bone-dim, or --c-high so contrast is ≥4.5:1 against the chip background. Keep --cherry-hi for non-text accents if needed.

findings.title: Hero poster preload omits ?v=MEDIA_REV
rebuttalsChecked: Metadata icons already point at /poster/hero.jpg so preload matching that path is consistent — rejected: posterSrc/videoSrc/framePath all gained ?v=MEDIA_REV at HEAD while the LCP preload did not
Browsers may coalesce identical bytes — rejected: the URLs differ, so the cache keys differ under immutable /poster

evidence.detail: <link rel="preload" as="image" href="/poster/hero.jpg" fetchPriority="high" /> with no query. icons.icon/apple also use /poster/hero.jpg.
MEDIA_REV is 'd2560b'. posterSrc(slug) returns `/poster/${slug}.jpg?v=${MEDIA_REV}`.
poster={posterSrc(SLUG)} so the <video> poster URL includes ?v=d2560b.
Image() for the poster uses posterSrc(slug), a different URL than the HTML preload.
/poster is Cache-Control public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Contract: content change requires a name/query change.

findings.impact: First paint can fetch the LCP still twice (unversioned preload vs versioned poster). After a MEDIA_REV bump, returning tabs can keep the old immutable poster while the film URL is new.
findings.remediation: Point the preload (and metadata icons) at posterSrc('hero') so every poster request shares the cache-bust query.

findings.title: README animation and media claims are stale versus current code and assets
rebuttalsChecked: 112 could mean source frames before trim — rejected: FRAME_COUNTS, manifest.json, and public/frames/display all equal 56
724 could include unused frames — rejected: 56+56+104+120+48+100+64+120=668, which is 724 minus the old extra 56 Display frames
1600 px could still describe every sequence — rejected: Display frame_0001.jpg is 2560×1440 at HEAD; the other seven sequences remain 1600-wide
Adjacent-frame blending could still exist behind a flag — rejected: createFrameRenderer paints a single nearest frame at alpha 1; blend/QUANT removed at HEAD

evidence.detail: Display listed as pinned scroll-scrub (112 frames). Performance table lists 8 frame sequences (724 frames), 1600 px. Animation approach still claims adjacent-frame blending / cross-dissolve. Chrome section claims a 2s first-visit / 400ms repeat loader floor. Live Lighthouse attributed to https://rezerv-ui-animation.vercel.app. Unset NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL claimed to ship a placeholder origin.
FRAME_COUNTS.display is 56; CLIP_SIZE.display is [2560, 1440]; sequence totals 668 frames.
display.frames is 56.
Directory contains 56 JPEG files (frame_0001.jpg through frame_0056.jpg) at 2560×1440.
NEAREST FRAME: paints one still; comments state adjacent-frame cross-dissolve was removed because it ghosted rotating products.
COUNT_FIRST_S=2.4, COUNT_REPEAT_S=1.2, BRAND_FIRST_MS=1100, BRAND_REPEAT_MS=700, MAX_VISIBLE_MS=8000 — not 2s / 400ms.
FALLBACK_URL is https://rezerv-ui-animation.vercel.app; SITE.url already defaults to production.
requestedUrl is https://iphone-18-concept-rust.vercel.app/, not the README production URL.
HEAD 50cbfc0 message: Update media assets and adjust frame counts. Parent Display was 112 frames; README 112/724/1600/cross-dissolve lines were not updated.

findings.impact: The Part 1 README is a scored deliverable. A reviewer following it will grade a blending pipeline, a 112-frame 1600 px Display sequence, and Lighthouse on an origin the reports were not captured on.
findings.remediation: Update README Display to 56 frames at 2560 px, sequence total to 668, replace adjacent-frame blending with nearest-frame + lerp/repaint-gating, correct preloader timings, and attribute live Lighthouse to the origin stored in the JSON (or recapture against rezerv-ui-animation.vercel.app). Drop the leftover claim that unset NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ships a placeholder.

findings.title: Reduced-motion still waits on the 4K hero film
rebuttalsChecked: Static tier already skips pin, scrub, and autoplay — true, but that only pauses playback after the film has been used as the preloader gate
LazyVideo correctly skips promoting preload when !canAutoplay — true for section clips; the hero is not LazyVideo and hard-codes preload=auto
8s fail-open bounds the wait — intentional for failures, not a reduced-motion skip; visitors who asked for less motion still start the 4K fetch

evidence.detail: prefers-reduced-motion returns STATIC: canScrub/canPin/canAutoplay false. No flag to skip hero fetch.
Always attaches canplaythrough / readyState>=3 / buffered progress. No useMotionPolicy guard. Finishes only on ready or error.
preload="auto" is declarative and never mutated. useHeroPreload always runs. canAutoplay false only pauses after entranceUnlocked.
CLIP_SIZE.hero is [3840, 2160]. Comment: hero has no mobile sibling because preload=auto must start before the tier resolves.
Contrast: !canAutoplay returns before IntersectionObserver promotes preload — the pattern the hero does not use.

findings.impact: Visitors with prefers-reduced-motion still wait on the loading curtain until the 4K hero buffers (or the 8s cap), which undercuts the Part 1 reduced-motion bonus.
findings.remediation: On the static tier, call preloadStore.setReady() from the poster and keep the hero at preload="none" (or omit the film) so the curtain does not wait on the 4K download.

findings.title: Browsers request /favicon.ico and receive 404
rebuttalsChecked: Metadata icons already point at /poster/hero.jpg — true, but user agents still request /favicon.ico by convention
Could be a Lighthouse-only request — reproduced on lab localhost and live origin reports

evidence.detail: icons.icon and apple point at /poster/hero.jpg; no /favicon.ico.
No favicon.ico (or other favicon.* ) in the tree.
errors-in-console: Failed to load resource 404 http://localhost:3100/favicon.ico. This is the Best Practices 96 deduction.
Same 404 against https://iphone-18-concept-rust.vercel.app/favicon.ico.

findings.impact: Every navigation logs a console error; Lighthouse Best Practices stays at 96 solely from this miss. Tabs that ignore metadata icons show a generic mark.
findings.remediation: Add public/favicon.ico (and optionally app icons) that match the existing hero poster, or add a rewrite/header that serves the poster at /favicon.ico.

findings.title: UltraTransition leftover inline opacity/transform on teardown
rebuttalsChecked: GSAP kill() reverts inline styles — rejected: animation is undefined; onUpdate writes element.style directly, so kill does not clear opacity/transform
CSS rest opacity:1 would win — rejected: inline style beats the stylesheet until cleared
canPin never flips mid-session — rejected: motionPolicy refreshes on 768/reduced-motion matchMedia and rebuilds this effect

evidence.detail: onUpdate sets card.style.opacity = 0.3+0.7p and transform scale(0.94+0.06p). Cleanup only sets willChange=auto and tween.kill().
.card rest opacity: 1; comment says that rest is for mobile and reduced motion where no ramp runs.

findings.impact: If canPin flips while the ramp is mid-progress, the only bright clip on the page can stay dimmed and scaled instead of the documented full-opacity rest state.
findings.remediation: Clear opacity and transform (or GSAP clearProps) on teardown; explicitly set the rest state when !canPin.

findings.title: Failed frame load drops pin / document height jump
rebuttalsChecked: Pin-on-mount already keeps height constant — true on the happy path; failed is in useGSAP deps and skips/kills the pin
Video fallback is the designed recovery — true for visuals, but stacked layout is a different box and is explicitly 'not a pinnable box'
Happy-path Playwright height tests would catch this — rejected: they do not cover a 404 JPEG
A single missing JPEG might still paint the rest — rejected: loadOne onerror rejects; loadFrames Promise.all fails the whole set

evidence.detail: Comment: pin is created on mount so document height is constant (historical 1620–2520px jumps). Guard: if (!section || !policy.canPin || failed) return; failed is a useGSAP dependency, so a late fail kills the pin.
loadOne img.onerror rejects Frame failed: ${src}. loadFrames awaits Promise.all of workers, so one 404 rejects the entire sequence.
mode === 'video' && videoLayout === 'stacked' switches data-layout and mounts LazyVideo instead of the pinned canvas stage.
All eight scrub sections pass videoLayout="stacked" (Colors, Display, CameraSensor, A20Pro, ProVsProMax, UltraHero, UltraColors, Fold).

findings.impact: A CDN miss or a drifted FRAME_COUNTS value collapses that section's pin spacer while the visitor is on the page — the class of height jump pin-on-mount was written to prevent. Confidence 88: forced by code, not reproduced with a live 404 this run.
findings.remediation: Keep the spacer or an overlay fallback so height stays constant; do not pin the stacked box. Optionally tolerate a missing JPEG without rejecting the whole FrameSet.

rejectedCandidates.title: Preloader canplaythrough / readyState>=3 / 8s fail-open
rejectedCandidates.reason: Intentional. readyState>=3 is the documented warm-cache check; MAX_VISIBLE_MS=8000 is explicit fail-open ('nobody waits forever'). Cold path still listens for canplaythrough. README 2s/400ms mismatch belongs in QA-DOCS-001, not as a loader bug.

rejectedCandidates.title: Hash URLs stripped; /#section never lands
rejectedCandidates.reason: Intentional contract. layout.tsx blocking script and ScrollReset strip location.hash; tests/scroll.spec.ts requires /#battery to stay at top; README Chrome table matches.

rejectedCandidates.title: Landscape phones width>=768 get canScrub and fetch /frames/
rejectedCandidates.reason: Tablet contract is min-width: 768px, not UA. README + motionPolicy + Playwright 390 vs 834 match. Landscape >=768 is tablet by design.

rejectedCandidates.title: CHECKOUT_ABSENT
rejectedCandidates.reason: No cart, checkout, payment, auth, use server, route handlers, or middleware. Static landing page. Confirmed absence, not a defect.

rejectedCandidates.title: Insufficient contrast on --bone-faint text
rejectedCandidates.reason: Lab Lighthouse used #55534f. Current tokens use #8a8780. Rejected.

rejectedCandidates.title: Missing full Content-Security-Policy
rejectedCandidates.reason: Documented static-prerender tradeoff in next.config.mjs. No user input, no auth, no checkout. Residual risk recorded in limitations, not a verified defect.

rejectedCandidates.title: YouTube embed XSS / third-party script
rejectedCandidates.reason: videoId is a compile-time constant; youtube-nocookie host; iframe mounts only while the dialog is open.

rejectedCandidates.title: Lab mobile Lighthouse performance 61 as a current ship blocker
rejectedCandidates.reason: Live-origin reports are 98/100. Hero 4K preload is an intentional preloader gate for motion-on visitors. Recorded as rubric UNVERIFIED for throttled lab, not a verified functional defect. Reduced-motion still waiting on that film is QA-A11Y-003.
